title: Why Medieval Courts Put Animals on Trial
title_alt: The Pig That Was Put on Trial (And Why It Happened)
hook: In 1386, a pig was dressed in a man's clothes and executed after a real court trial. It wasn't a joke — for centuries, European courts put animals on trial.
summary: Pigs, bulls, rats, a rooster and even weevils got summonses, lawyers and verdicts. We follow the Pig of Falaise, the lawyer who defended rats (and blamed the cats), the rooster burned for laying an egg, and the weevils who were offered their own land — then reveal the surprising reason church courts kept holding these trials.
pinned: Which trial surprised you most — the pig, the rats' lawyer, the rooster, or the weevils' land deal? 🐷🐀🐓🪲 What why should Wy answer next?
